targetText:
Typical of the old capitalism, when free competition held
 undivided sway, was the export of goods. Typical of the latest
 stage of capitalism, when monopolies rule, is the export of
 capital.
summary: Under old competitive capitalism, nations exported physical manufactured goods. Under monopoly capitalism, wealthy nations export financial capital (loans and foreign investments) to extract perpetual dividends.
context: Instead of selling finished products to developing countries, rich nations invest surplus capital in foreign mines, infrastructure, and factories to capture high profit margins and lock those countries into debt dependence.

targetText:
surplus capital will be utilised
 not for the purpose of raising the standard of living of the
 masses in a given country
summary: Capitalists invest surplus wealth abroad where profits are highest, rather than spending it to eliminate poverty or improve public services at home.
context: Lenin refutes reformists who claim capitalists will use excess profits to end domestic poverty. Because capitalism is driven by profit rates, surplus wealth naturally flows wherever labor is cheapest and raw materials are most abundant.

summary: Foreign investment in developing nations yields superprofits because land, wages, and raw materials are far cheaper than in wealthy industrial nations.
context: This economic reality drives modern outsourcing and foreign corporate extraction, where multinational corporations locate factories and mines in low-wage countries to maximize shareholder returns.
